target_customer: E-commerce merchants, marketplaces and software platforms that need to integrate carrier shipping
problem: Integrating with each shipping carrier meant dealing with dated carrier APIs; EasyPost offers one API for rates, labels, tracking and insurance.
business_model: Usage-based API (per label and tracking fees)

founders.name: Jarrett Streebin
founders.background_notes: Credited with founding EasyPost in 2012 on the company about page; no co-founders named there or on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Normalizing many carrier APIs and label formats behind one RESTful API was tedious integration work with dated carrier technology, but standard web engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Once integrated into customer checkout and fulfillment flows the API is sticky, and carrier rate relationships and the integration breadth take time to replicate, though rivals could copy the wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent postage vendors did not absorb the wedge; EasyPost remained independent and its own comparison pages position it against Stamps.com, Endicia and Pitney Bowes.

market_need_then: The 2013 seed coverage described it as a Stripe for shipping with transactions doubling every month, indicating developer demand for a simple shipping API.

identity.logo: Wordmark and brand symbol created in an agency rebrand with Moving Brands (undated)
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and simple, centered on making shipping easy

brand_strength.rationale: A Moving Brands case study says the company had been through several unsuccessful rebrands before settling on a new identity; the descriptive name says what it does but is generic.

outcome_analysis: EasyPost raised an 850 thousand dollar seed in 2013 when transactions were doubling monthly, then a large Series A reported in 2018 at a roughly 420 million dollar valuation. Developer-led API integration created switching costs, and it grew to hundreds of employees. It remains independent, with a 2026 listing of a partial stake foreclosure sale that is unverified.
notes: Series A amount conflicts across aggregators: 49.5M, 50M, 58.5M and 63.03M; date June or September 2018; a separate 9M Series A in 2017 with Initialized and Section Partners is reported by one aggregator. Only the valuation estimate (Sacra, aggregators) is recorded and the amount is left null because no primary release was found. The 2020 Ruby Has deal concerned a different entity named EasyPost Fulfillment Services. Competitor search found Shippo (launched 2013 per an undated source) but no source dated near the batch, so the list is empty.
